channel.title: Economy
channel.description: Find the latest economic news, current events and headlines, as well as blogs and video from CNBC.com.

item.title: Liesman: Why Greenspan could bet on productivity — and Warsh needs to hike
item.description: Alan Greenspan famously held the line on interest rates because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet boom. Why can't Kevin Warsh do the same?

item.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October, raising the 2027 stakes for the central bank
item.description: The personal consumption expenditures price index was expected to show an annual inflation rate of 3.8% in October, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

item.title: Even the price of toys is on the rise. How Americans are scaling back holiday plans
item.description: U.S. consumers face higher food, travel and gift costs in 2026 as inflation and Iran-war energy shocks pressure holiday budgets.

item.title: ‘Ready for any storm’: UAE minister optimistic on economy as IMF lifts forecast
item.description: The UAE is optimistic about achieving 7%-8% economic growth next year, banking on a "different" economic model.

item.title: Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist
item.description: The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3.

item.title: Why France is at risk of recession — and what could keep it out of one
item.description: Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin told CNBC he still expects growth, pointing to resilience in sectors including defense, aerospace and electricity.

item.title: Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was becoming the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia— until he reversed course

item.title: Tech outages are fueling a new doomsday economy
item.description: Recent technology outages have left some worried about AI cyberattacks and the U.S. electricity grid. The doomsday economy is heating up as a result.

item.title: Japan core inflation soars to highest this year as energy subsidy expiry pushes up consumer prices
item.description: The core inflation figure — which strips out prices of food — was lower than the 2.3% expected by Reuters-polled economists.

item.title: Southeast Asia’s data center boom leaned on Chinese demand. New U.S. rules put that pipeline at risk
item.description: The rules require data centers in Southeast Asia to seek U.S. approval to buy advanced AI chips, threatening to slow a build-out fueled heavily on Chinese demand.

item.title: Record diesel prices drive UK inflation to 1-year high of 3.6%
item.description: It put the U.K.'s annual inflation rate at a 1-year high.

item.title: Japan exports in October surge 20.5%, beating estimates on robust chip shipments
item.description: Semiconductor shipments spiked almost 50% year on year.

item.title: St. Louis Fed's Musalem says four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months
item.description: The forecast represents one of the most hawkish views among policymakers.

item.title: Peterson: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means
item.description: Kevin Warsh sees AI at a turning point. He faces tough questions on jobs and interest rates.

item.title: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracts in third-quarter as elevated energy costs bite
item.description: Energy subsidies for households had reportedly expired in September, exposing the economy to the higher energy prices brought about by the Iran war.

item.title: AI risks are the biggest threat to the financial system, Fed survey finds
item.description: The report comes with Wall Street on edge over high-flying AI hyperscalers, while communities are on alert for the rapid spread of data centers.

item.title: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, putting annual rate at 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years
item.description: The producer price index was expected to increase 0.4% in October, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

item.title: Bessent blames Lutnick’s Commerce as he slams Nvidia chip ‘leakage’ to China
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO days after admitting to an affair following scrutiny of his relationship with a woman reportedly deemed a Chinese spy.

item.title: UK economy expands 0.7% in third quarter as AI provides 'extra engine of growth'
item.description: The U.K. economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter of the year, in line with estimates.

item.title: Peterson: Nvidia’s leadership crisis tests the chipmaker’s role as the ‘central bank of AI’
item.description: The tech giant's web of ties to other companies is raising the possibility that it could do far-reaching economic and financial damage.

item.title: Consumers are showing signs of strain even as they keep spending, CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor shows
item.description: Retail sales rose at their slowest pace in nearly a year in October as American consumers showed signs of strain from high prices.

item.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed's inflation fight
item.description: The report comes at a critical juncture for the Federal Reserve as it considers its next move regarding interest rates.

item.title: China's goods surplus tops $1 trillion for a second year amid calls for Beijing to rebalance trade
item.description: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion as of October, potentially intensifying complaints from trading partners already wary over the glut of cheap Chinese goods.

item.title: 3 unexpected reasons the October jobs report was so strong
item.description: October's jobs report blew past economist forecasts. Here are three reasons.

item.title: A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect
item.description: The CPI headline reading is expected to show an increase of 0.3% while the core is forecast to increase 0.2%.

item.title: China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years as consumer measure slows
item.description: The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

item.title: A disturbing employment trend is hiding beneath the latest strong job numbers
item.description: The average jobless worker's bout of unemployment surpassed 27 weeks in October, the highest outside of the pandemic period in a decade.

item.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%
item.description: Nonfarm payrolls were expected to increase by 59,000 in October as the unemployment rate was expected to hold steady at 4.2%.

item.title: The October jobs report is out Friday. Here's everything to expect
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the October nonfarm payrolls report Friday at 8:30 a.m. ET.

item.title: Here's what the Democratic election rout could mean for the U.S. economy
item.description: The biggest forces shaping the economy aren't going to change just because the party in power did.
